candidates.description: Nick Holonyak Jr. demonstrated the first practical visible-spectrum light-emitting diode at General Electric.

candidates.name: satellite-navigation-transit
candidates.description: The U.S. Navy launched Transit, the first satellite navigation system, a precursor to GPS.

candidates.name: great-leap-forward
candidates.description: Mao launched a radical campaign to rapidly industrialize China, resulting in history's deadliest famine with an estimated 30-45 million deaths.

candidates.name: bay-of-pigs
candidates.description: A CIA-backed invasion of Cuba by exiles failed disastrously.

candidates.name: first-arcade-video-game
candidates.description: Computer Space, created by Nolan Bushnell, became the first commercially sold arcade video game.

candidates.name: nasdaq-launches
candidates.description: NASDAQ began as the world's first electronic stock market, trading shares through computers instead of a floor.

candidates.name: first-one-day-international-1971
candidates.description: After a washed-out Test, Australia beat England at Melbourne in the first One Day International, watched by 46,000 fans.

candidates.name: first-ct-scan-patient
candidates.friendly_name: First CT Scan of a Patient
candidates.description: A London hospital used a rotating X-ray machine and a computer to image a woman's brain slice by slice.

candidates.name: kent-state-shootings
candidates.description: Ohio National Guard killed four students during anti-Vietnam War protests at Kent State University.

candidates.name: watergate-break-in
candidates.description: Burglars connected to Nixon's reelection campaign broke into Democratic headquarters, starting the scandal.

candidates.name: pocket-calculator
candidates.description: Handheld electronic calculators replaced slide rules and mechanical adding machines.

candidates.name: alekseyev-600kg-total-1970
candidates.description: Soviet weightlifter Vasily Alekseyev became the first man to total 600 kg across the three lifts, starting a run of 80 world records.

candidates.name: world-trade-center-tops-out
candidates.description: The North Tower of New York's World Trade Center topped out, surpassing the Empire State Building as the tallest building on Earth.

candidates.name: kbo-league-founded-korea-1982
candidates.description: South Korea's professional KBO League launched with six franchises, opening its inaugural season in Seoul.

candidates.name: assassination-attempt-on-reagan
candidates.description: John Hinckley Jr. shot President Reagan outside a Washington hotel, seriously wounding him. Reagan recovered and served two full terms.

candidates.name: assassination-attempt-on-pope
candidates.description: Turkish gunman Mehmet Ali Agca shot Pope John Paul II in St. Peter's Square. The Pope survived and later forgave his would-be assassin.

candidates.name: aids-epidemic-recognized
candidates.description: The CDC first reported cases of what would become the AIDS pandemic.

candidates.name: trivial-pursuit-launched
candidates.description: Two Canadians launched Trivial Pursuit, a board game of general-knowledge questions that became a sensation.

candidates.name: microwave-meals-spread
candidates.description: Affordable countertop microwave ovens reached homes, changing how families reheated and cooked food.

candidates.name: live-aid
candidates.description: A dual-venue rock concert raised millions for Ethiopian famine relief.

candidates.name: gorbachev-becomes-leader
candidates.description: Mikhail Gorbachev became Soviet leader, initiating reforms that would ultimately end the Cold War.

candidates.name: glasnost-perestroika
candidates.description: Gorbachev introduced policies of openness and restructuring to reform the Soviet system.

candidates.name: first-ozone-hole-discovered
candidates.description: Scientists discovered severe ozone depletion over Antarctica, leading to global action on CFCs.

candidates.name: mexico-city-earthquake
candidates.description: A powerful earthquake killed over 10,000 people in the Mexican capital.

candidates.name: nevado-del-ruiz
candidates.description: A volcanic mudflow buried the Colombian town of Armero, killing 23,000.

candidates.name: unicode-standard-released
candidates.description: Unicode assigned every character a unique code, letting computers handle the world's writing systems.

candidates.name: nevermind-album
candidates.description: Nirvana's album brought grunge and alternative rock to the mainstream.

candidates.name: pgp-encryption-released
candidates.description: Phil Zimmermann gave away Pretty Good Privacy, putting strong encryption in ordinary hands and drawing a federal investigation.

candidates.name: nelson-mandela-freed
candidates.description: The anti-apartheid leader was freed after 27 years in prison.

candidates.name: anc-unbanned
candidates.description: South African government lifted ban on ANC and released Nelson Mandela, beginning end of apartheid.

candidates.name: first-exoplanet
candidates.description: Astronomers discovered the first planets orbiting a star outside our solar system.

candidates.name: black-wednesday-pound
candidates.description: Speculators forced the British pound out of Europe's exchange rate system, costing the government billions.

candidates.name: przewalski-horses-rewilded
candidates.description: Captive bred Przewalski's horses were released onto the Mongolian steppe, restoring the last truly wild horse.

candidates.name: mosaic-web-browser
candidates.description: NCSA Mosaic launched as the first widely popular graphical web browser, making the Web accessible to ordinary users.

candidates.name: genetically-modified-crop
candidates.description: The Flavr Savr tomato became the first genetically modified food sold, opening debate over GM crops.

candidates.name: rwanda-tribunal-established
candidates.description: The United Nations created a court to prosecute those responsible for the Rwandan genocide.

candidates.name: microsoft-windows-95
candidates.description: Microsoft launched Windows 95, bringing the graphical desktop interface to the masses.

candidates.name: mp3-audio-format
candidates.description: The Fraunhofer Institute released the MP3 audio format, enabling digital music distribution.

candidates.name: rugby-union-turns-professional
candidates.description: The IRB declared rugby union an open game, ending amateurism a century after the split that created rugby league.

candidates.name: clinton-first-inauguration
candidates.description: A young Arkansas governor became the first baby boomer president, in a ceremony featuring a poem by Maya Angelou.

candidates.name: usb-standard
candidates.description: The Universal Serial Bus standard was released, simplifying how devices connect to computers.

candidates.name: tokyo-subway-attack
candidates.description: The Aum Shinrikyo cult released sarin gas on the Tokyo subway, killing 13.

candidates.name: wifi-standard
candidates.description: The IEEE 802.11 standard was released, enabling wireless internet that transformed how we connect.

candidates.name: deep-blue-beats-kasparov
candidates.description: IBM's Deep Blue defeated world champion Garry Kasparov, the first computer to beat a top human at chess.

candidates.name: settlers-of-catan-released
candidates.description: Klaus Teuber's Settlers of Catan launched in Germany, sparking a global revival of modern board gaming.

candidates.name: microsoft-windows-95
candidates.description: Microsoft launched Windows 95, bringing the graphical desktop interface to the masses.

candidates.name: apple-think-different-campaign
candidates.description: A tribute to rebels and visionaries, with black-and-white portraits, marked a computer maker's co-founder returning.

candidates.name: singapore-flyer
candidates.description: The world's largest observation wheel at the time opened.

candidates.name: western-union-ends-telegrams
candidates.description: The company that once dominated the telegraph quietly stopped sending telegrams, ending a long era of wired messages.

candidates.name: iphone-released
candidates.description: Apple's smartphone revolutionized mobile technology and communication.

candidates.name: asean-charter
candidates.description: Southeast Asian nations adopted a charter giving ASEAN legal status.

candidates.name: lisbon-treaty
candidates.description: The EU reformed its institutions and created a permanent president.

candidates.name: virginia-tech-shooting
candidates.description: Gunman killed 32 people at Virginia Tech in the deadliest school shooting in US history.

candidates.name: wikileaks-cables
candidates.description: WikiLeaks released thousands of classified US diplomatic cables, embarrassing governments worldwide.

candidates.name: danyang-kunshan-grand-bridge
candidates.description: The world's longest bridge opened as part of Beijing-Shanghai rail line.

candidates.name: death-steve-jobs
candidates.description: Apple co-founder Steve Jobs died of cancer, mourned worldwide for revolutionizing personal technology.

candidates.name: fukushima-disaster
candidates.description: An earthquake and tsunami caused meltdowns at a Japanese nuclear plant.

candidates.name: instagram-launched
candidates.description: The photo-sharing app that transformed social media was released.

candidates.name: chilean-mine-rescue
candidates.description: All 33 miners trapped underground for 69 days were rescued in a dramatic televised operation.
